subject: Public Comment for July 1, 2025 Council Meeting
comment: Dear Council Members and City Recorder, I am submitting this comment to formally enter my prepared remarks from the July 1, 2025 Salt Lake City Council meeting into the official public record. Due to the two-minute limit, my live comment was cut off just before the final lines, so I am providing the full intended version here as prepared and delivered. For context and clarity, I have also included the full text of the relevant Salt Lake City and Utah Code sections cited in my statement. I respectfully request that this text be attached in full to the official meeting record for transparency. Prepared Statement Happy Fiscal New Year, Council. I'm not here for that, but because today also marks two other events this council and taxpayers should not ignore. First, today is day one of the County's new 0.2% sales tax increase. When combined with the State's Jan. 1st 0.2% increase and this Council's own 0.5% downtown revitalization tax, city sales taxes are now nearly a full percentage point higher than a year ago today — putting Salt Lake City's rate higher than even San Francisco's. Second, today is the city's 2025 campaign contribution filing date. In that connection, with campaign season upon us and because this body approved the largest share of the sales-tax increases — and has levied nearly $3 billion total to benefit billionaire investors — voters deserve full transparency about any perks, gifts, or exclusive access that influenced your decisions. For this election cycle, there are two conflicts deserving full disclosure and explanation. First is a trip to the L.A. LIVE Entertainment District — Ryan Smith said at the new Miller Lite arena's first press conference that public officials traveled to LA with him. Who from this Council attended? What were the travel details — and who paid for flights, lodging, or any other perks? Second, within days of your vote to approve the billion-dollar arena-renovation and downtown-development tax, which members of this Council attended the Hockey team's historic first game at Delta Center? I have reason to believe at least one of you running for reelection attended the game in SEG's private skybox. Even cheap seats to the game were hard to get and priced well beyond most voters' budgets, with some tickets reselling for thousands. Even councilors who paid the team some form of face value or so-called "fair market" price for this exclusive access should disclose it. Voters deserve the details to judge for themselves the extent of any influence or reward. Both Salt Lake City Code (§2.44.080) and Utah Code (§67-16-5) contain restrictions on public servants accepting gifts or access that might influence — or appear to reward — official actions. Release receipts. Report it in this campaign disclosure cycle. Don't just follow the letter of the law — honor its spirit too. That's the least taxpayers should expect when they're paying more at the register to cover costs for pro sports teams' multi-billion-dollar development. Thank you. Appendix – Relevant Code Sections Salt Lake City Code §2.44.080 – Gifts Prohibited 2.44.080: No city officer or employee shall solicit or accept any gift, gratuity, favor, entertainment, loan, or any other thing of monetary value from any person who is seeking to obtain contractual or other business or financial relations with the city, or who has interests that may be substantially affected by the performance or nonperformance of the officer's or employee's official duties. Utah Code §67-16-5 – Acceptance of Gifts, Compensation, or Loans 67-16-5(1): It is an offense for a public officer or public employee, under circumstances not constituting a violation of Section 63G-6a-2404, to knowingly receive, accept, take, seek, or solicit, directly or indirectly for themselves or another, a gift of substantial value or a substantial economic benefit tantamount to a gift that would tend improperly to influence a reasonable person in the person's position to depart from the faithful and impartial discharge of the person's public duties. 67-16-5(2): It is an offense for a public officer or public employee to knowingly receive, accept, take, seek, or solicit, directly or indirectly for themselves or another, a gift of substantial value or a substantial economic benefit tantamount to a gift: (a) given for the purpose of rewarding the public officer or public employee for official action taken; or (b) given for a purpose related to the public officer's or public employee's position or duties. Respectfully submitted for the official record, Scott Johnson

subject: Voicemail to City Council
comment: Hi my name is Kai Barrera, I live in District 4 and work in a business that is directly across from the Ballpark. NEXT proposal plan, a company called Davis Audio Visual. There are 3 things that I see with this plan that are not being properly addressed for the Ballpark area. 1. I don't think this plan truly considers the long term health and success of the CURRENT Ballpark residents. I feel that is more focused on the future higher class people that they would like to move into this area. The reason he because there isn't much information about the housing units being provided, how many will be below market rate and available for low income individuals. I believe, if this plans goes on as it is now, it will increase the cost of living in the area and disproportionally affect those already living in the area and gentrify them out of the area. I think it needs to focus how this plan will enrich and add value to the people who are living and not drive them out. Another thing that I don't think has been talked about at all is how will this affect local business. In 2 ways I think it may not be fully considered what the construction may look like in the area. I would hate to see a similar situation that is happening in Sugar House now. Where lots of business are struggling to stay open or have already closed their doors due to relentless construction and inaccessible foot and vehicle access which is causing more damage to the community in the long term. Once those businesses are gone, they never come back. They usually get replaced by box stores or larger chains. One thing I think would be very beneficial is to consider what businesses are already in the area, like the one I work for Davis Audio Visual. They provide services for venues and events. Which is perfect to add for the Ballpark plan. They have been there for decades and we have not had anyone reach out to us to be involved in the plan even though there is an event venue right down from the business front door. I think if there was more community activation with the businesses at store level and more talk about how to get more local business, artists and community members engaged or even funding grants to start businesses in the Ballpark area. That would be a huge step in the right direction to create more sustainability, more economic long term generational probability for the Ballpark area and it's current residents. I think the last thing I want to touch on it how these feel, more specially the creek park area on the north part of the plan. I don't see that area being comfortable to live or be in, especially with the hotel on the street across from it. I see this turning 13th south into a very congested area. Which would mean lots of vehicle traffic and the Creek Park would be very loud to be in with the air and noise pollution from all of the vehicles.

subject: Voicemail to City Council
comment: Hi my name is Nikki Doanne. I have lived in SLC my whole life. this has to do with the Ballpark plan. 1 thing I think the plan is really good for is the walkability. Having nature and it is good to native plants as well. One of the big aspects, that is just as important as housing and making housing affordable, is there are a lot of local businesses that don't have much. If we are serious about protecting this community, one the things we need to do is interrogate the local businesses in that area. If not, they are going to get pushed out and it will be brutal. I don't think any of these business owners have the means to combat or fight that or to get any place. But if we are integrating the local businesses, we need to keep rent lowered for them as well. I don't think there is a ethical way to bring in more local business that isn't in this area. I don't think it is ethical to charge these businesses a bunch of money up front either. I hope this is taken into extreme consideration, especially since this helps the community that is already there and the people that are there and truly make this a space for everyone. Thank you.
